title: Yankees clinch playoff spot, but bigger AL East question looms
content:
MINNEAPOLIS — The New York Yankees are going to the playoffs again, clinching a postseason spot Monday when the Toronto Blue Jays lost 6-5 to the Detroit Tigers. It happened as the Yankees were up big late against the Minnesota Twins, whom they went on to defeat 8-3.

When the Yankees celebrate, they will soak the walls and the carpet of the visitors clubhouse at Target Field with champagne and beer.

But should they aim higher?

Manager Aaron Boone and the Yankees’ front office have to decide whether it’s smart to prioritize passing the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East or if they should decelerate, setting their sights on winning home-field advantage in the best-of-three wild-card round while learning everything they can about their evolving roster.

Once the champagne stops burning the Yankees’ eyes, they may need to face an unkind truth. Entering Monday, they were four games behind the Rays and had just a 9.6 percent chance of winning the division, according to FanGraphs. They were also 4 1/2 games ahead of the third-place Boston Red Sox, over whom they hold the tiebreaker.

Just 12 regular-season games remain for the Yankees. Four of them will come against the Rays at home, starting next Tuesday with a split doubleheader. The Yankees are 3-6 against Tampa Bay this season, and must sweep next week’s series to win the season series and own the tiebreaker between the clubs. The Rays have been swept once in a four-game series this season — by the Red Sox in July.

The Yankees surely would prefer to win the division and skip the wild-card round altogether. The benefits are obvious. With a division win, they would also secure the best record in the AL, which would give them home-field advantage until the World Series.

It would also give them nearly a week of rest, which would be particularly valuable for their late-inning trio of Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn and closer David Bednar, who have been worked hard.

It would give the Yankees a chance to set up their starting rotation for the AL Division Series, and it would give another week of preparation to Aaron Judge, who returned Sept. 8 after missing more than three months on the injured list. Not to mention, it would give them more time to see if Giancarlo Stanton (calf strains) could be a possibility for the playoff roster.

When the Yankees went to the World Series in 2024, they had the AL’s best regular-season record and were able to skip the wild-card round.

But last season, they tied the Toronto Blue Jays for the best record in the AL, and since they lost the tiebreaker to Toronto, they had to battle the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, and needed all three games to beat them. They went on to get boat-raced 3-1 by the Blue Jays in the best-of-five Division Series.

By clinching a playoff spot Monday, the Yankees notched their 60th postseason appearance in franchise history, 21 more than the Los Angeles Dodgers, who have the second most at 39. It also means they are one of only two teams to make the playoffs in at least nine of the last 10 years, along with the Dodgers.
